author: John C. Maxwell
text: A leader is one who knows the way, goes the way, and shows the way.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Leadership is not about titles, positions, or flowcharts. It is about one life influencing another.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: All great achievers are given multiple reasons to believe they are failures. But in spite of that they persevere.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: The best leaders are those who understand that their power comes not from their position, but from their ability to empower others.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: The greatest danger to most organizations is not external threats, but internal weaknesses.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: The bottom line in leadership isn't how far we advance ourselves but how far we advance others.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Good leaders stop bossing people around and start encouraging them.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Leaders have to deal simultaneously with people issues and business issues, and they need to be able to do both effectively. That's an art.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: If you want to be a leader, the good news is that you can do it. Everyone has the potential, but it isn't accomplished overnight.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Champions don't become champions in the ring—they are merely recognized there.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Nobody achieves anything great by giving the minimum. No teams win championships without making sacrifices and giving their best.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Every message that people receive is filtered through the messenger who delivers it.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Great leaders always seem to embody two seemingly disparate qualities. They are both highly visionary and highly practical.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: When people respect you as a person, they admire you. When they respect you as a friend, they love you. When they respect you as a leader, they follow you.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Your values are the soul of your leadership, and they drive your behavior.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: To be effective, leaders must always be learners.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Everything rises and falls on leadership.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Leadership is influence. Nothing more, nothing less.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: What happens to me doesn't have to determine what happens within me.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: How well you lead determines how well you succeed.

author: John C. Maxwell
text: Good management of bad experiences leads to great personal growth.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Become the kind of leader that people would follow voluntarily; even if you had no title or position.
work: The Great Big Book of Wisdom

author: Brian Tracy
text: Leadership is the ability to get extraordinary achievement from ordinary people.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Integrity is the most valuable and respected quality of leadership. Always keep your word.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Superior leaders are willing to admit a mistake and cut their losses. Be willing to admit that you've changed your mind. Don't persist when the original decision turns out to be a poor one.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The glue that holds all relationships together–including the relationship between the leader and the led–is trust, and trust is based on integrity.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The true test of leadership is how well you function in a crisis.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The key responsibility of leadership is to think about the future. No one else can do it for you.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The potential of the average person is like a huge ocean unsailed, a new continent unexplored, a world of possibilities waiting to be released and channeled toward some great good.

author: Brian Tracy
text: A clear vision, backed by definite plans, gives you a tremendous feeling of confidence and personal power.
work: The Great Big Book of Wisdom

author: Brian Tracy
text: People who take a long view of their lives and careers always seem to make much better decisions about their time and activities than people who give very little thought to the future.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Leaders never use the word failure. They look upon setbacks as learning experiences.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Leaders think and talk about the solutions. Followers think and talk about the problems.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The three 'C's' of leadership are consideration, caring, and courtesy. Be polite to everyone.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Practice Golden Rule Management in everything you do. Manage others the way you would like to be managed.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Leaders set high standards. Refuse to tolerate mediocrity or poor performance.

author: Brian Tracy
text: Move out of your comfort zone. You can only grow if you are willing to feel awkward and uncomfortable when you try something new.

author: Brian Tracy
text: The future belongs to the competent. Get good, get better, be the best!

author: Brian Tracy
text: Your life only gets better when you get better.

author: Brian Tracy
text: You are the architect of your own destiny; you are the master of your own fate; you are behind the steering wheel of your life.
work: The 21 Success Secrets of Self-Made Millionaires

author: Brian Tracy
text: Successful people are always looking for opportunities to help others. Unsuccessful people are always asking, "What's in it for me?"

author: Brian Tracy
text: The foundation of lasting self-confidence and self-esteem is excellence, mastery of your work.
work: The Great Big Book of Wisdom

author: Brian Tracy
text: Always give without remembering and always receive without forgetting.
work: The Great Big Book of Wisdom
